A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Add-One-In and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Relocated material can be matched, including the unchanged algorithm and three identical case-study images.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original fine-tuning comparisons, benchmark scores, selection-efficiency measurements, ablations and Chinese medical evaluation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds training-budget comparisons and initialization experiments in Appendices A.2–A.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same prompt-based greedy selection, random initialization, sampled candidate windows and update steps. K-means and KNN initializations are tested as ablation variants; the proposed algorithm itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, the four instruction-following test sets, MMLU, BBH, Hellaswag, and HuatuoGPT data with CMB evaluation. The additions vary sample budgets and initialization within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Main benchmark and medical comparator sets remain unchanged. The new initialization comparison in Table 9 adds Ours + Kmeans and Ours + KNN alongside the original random-initialized method and retained baselines. These are additional comparison variants, not standalone selection baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds 3K and 6K training-budget conditions to the existing 9K/52K benchmark comparison. Existing benchmark shot settings, GPT4o judging procedure and stated training configurations are retained.

E4.justification: v2 extends training-size sensitivity analysis to benchmark accuracy and adds random-versus-K-means/KNN initialization analysis using diversity and quality metrics. Existing window-size, selection-round, efficiency and case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are retained. New entries include Ours MMLU zero-shot scores of 22.30 and 22.70 at 3K and 6K, alongside the retained 9K score of 23.82. Table 9 adds K-means/KNN initialization results, including MTLD values of 9.0125 and 8.8721. These concern additional experimental conditions.

T1.justification: The marginal-gain formulation, LLM selection equation, approximation discussion, complexity argument and appendix metric formulas are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or mathematical assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim contribution-oriented selection balancing quality and diversity, reduced selection overhead, competitive subset performance and medical applicability. Replacing 'SOTA studies' with 'recent powerful studies' in the abstract does not substantively alter these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets initialization results as evidence of relative robustness and hypothesizes that limiting A′ to at most 20 elements reduces initialization's influence. Existing limitations concerning LLM biases, prompt and window choices, and online data remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies GPT3.5 in several experiment descriptions and the ablation table where v1 used the broader label ChatGPT. This adds model-identification detail without establishing a model replacement or rerun. Training details and resource URLs are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Psyche-R1, PsycoLLM, AgentMental and an emotion-understanding benchmark, broadening introductory application context. Core data-selection positioning remains stable. Li et al.'s 2024 preprint and 2025 ACL entry represent the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical edits, updates affiliations and correspondence information, adds acknowledgments and expands appendix explanations. Moving the algorithm and Random comparison into the main text also reorganizes the appendices, while the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the training-budget table and initialization Table 9, relocates and resizes Algorithm 1 and the Random-comparison figure, and enlarges the medical-results table. Existing plots and case images are retained. The budget table has conflicting captions numbered Table 6 and Table 7.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical understanding by extending budget-sensitivity evidence to benchmark accuracy and testing initialization choices. Making Algorithm 1 accessible in the main text also helps. These gains are qualified by underspecified initialization implementations and erroneous new IFD averages: 41.53/41.97 disagree with component-score means of approximately 41.81/42.16. The added evidence remains useful, but its reporting limits the improvement.
